summary:
--- PART 1/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "Parent (slot 11):" and "Parent slot 11: if op_d==0 return C" — the trace treats the parent strategy as the thing being revised, not a report.
STRATEGY: Parent starts C, cooperates forever vs always-C, defects vs always-D, retaliates to runs of D, uses cooperation-rate thresholds, and defects on the final round. The trace simulates parent against AlwaysC, AlwaysD, TFT, Grim, and population slots, then proposes adding late-game defection against always-cooperative opponents and adaptive classification.

--- PART 2/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So we can implement a late-game probe: around round 90-95, defect once. Then adapt based on response."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates if opponent has never defected, defects if opponent always defects, and otherwise uses a TFT-with-forgiveness rule. The trace simulates late-game probes against TFT, Grim, and AlwaysC, and proposes fixing the last-round defection and adding AlwaysC detection/exploitation.

--- PART 3/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So the safe improvement is just to defect on the last round." / "Thus, the main improvement is to fix the last-round defection."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates until the last round, with TFT-like retaliation/forgiveness and an early return for always-cooperating opponents. Simulated against AlwaysC, TFT, Grim, AlwaysD, and population/archive mixes. Changed by adding last-round defection at n==99 and removing random endgame defection.
